# Lua hook reference

<!-- Generated by scripts/gen-lua-hooks.py from the MUTATOR_HOOKABLE declarations. Do not edit. -->

Mods can subscribe to **172 hooks** of the server game code and **54 hooks** of the client game code (Xonotic's mutator hooks). On the server 59 have outputs a mod may change and 43 can be cancelled. How to use them, the tiers and the limits are in [PLUGIN_STANDARD.md](PLUGIN_STANDARD.md#hooks); the rest of the API is in [LUA_API.md](LUA_API.md).

```lua
-- a server mod
xt.hook("PlayerDies", function(h)
  print("player", h.target, "died, deathtype", h.deathtype)
end)
xt.hook("Damage_Calculate", function(h)
  h.damage = h.damage * 0.5     -- an output: needs the gamerules tier
end)
```

Each handler gets one table `h`. Every argument is in it three ways: under its position key, the type letter and the game's argument index (`e0`, `f4`, `s1`, `v2`, `i1`, `b5`); under the bare index (`h[4]`, as Insanotic's `ev[4]`); and, where the declaration names it plainly, under that name (`h.damage` is `h.f4` in `Damage_Calculate`). Types: `e` an entity number (a player's is their player id, 1..maxplayers; 0 is none; `xt.ent(n)` gives a live handle on the server), `f` number, `i` integer, `b` boolean, `v` `{x, y, z}`, `s` string.

**out** arguments are what the hook lets mutators change: set the field (any of its three names) and the game uses the new value (entities are never written). **Cancel**: where the game's own description says to return true, a handler returning `true` does that. On the server both need the `gamerules` tier; without it changes and return values are ignored. On the client a hook only changes this player's own screen, so the drawing hooks (`HUD_Draw_overlay`, `DrawCrosshair`, `DrawScoreboard`, ...) are writable with the standard tier and the others are read only.

Hooks caused by a mod's own API call (a `p:give` that fires `ItemTouch`, say) are not delivered to any mod: a mod never runs inside another mod's call.

## Client hooks

These exist only while this game's own client code runs (`xt.csqc() == "godnotic"`): in local games, on Godnotic servers, and on any server whose client code is the same as this game's. On a server that sends different client code, `xt.hook` still accepts the subscription and the handler never runs.

| Hook | Arguments | Cancel | What the game says |
|---|---|---|---|
| `BuildMutatorsString` | `s0` `mutator_string` in/out: mutator string |  | Appends ":mutatorname" to argument for logging |
| `BuildMutatorsPrettyString` | `s0` `mutator_string` in/out: mutator string |  | Appends ", Mutator name" to ret_string for display |
| `BuildGameplayTipsString` | `s0` `tips_string` in/out: tips string |  | Appends mutator string for displaying extra gameplay tips |
| `IsFlying` | `e0` in |  | - |
| `WP_Format` | `e0` in<br>`s1` in<br>`v2` out<br>`s3` out<br>`s4` out |  | - |
| `PlayerPhysics` | `e0` `player` in: player<br>`f1` `ticrate` in: ticrate |  | Called before any player physics, may adjust variables for movement, is run AFTER bot code and idle checking on the server |
| `PlayerJump` | `e0` `player` in: player<br>`f1` `jump_height` in/out: jump height<br>`b2` `multijump` in/out: multijump |  | Called when a player presses the jump key |
| `PM_Physics` | `e0` `player` in: player<br>`f1` `maxspeed_mod` in: maxspeed_mod<br>`f2` `tick_rate` in: tick rate |  | Called during player physics, allows adjusting the movement type used |

| `PlayerCanCrouch` | `e0` `player` in: player<br>`b1` `do_crouch` in/out: do_crouch |  | Decides whether a player can crouch or not |
| `CSQC_ConsoleCommand` | `s0` `command_name` in: command name<br>`i1` `argc` in: argc (also, argv() can be used)<br>`s2` `whole_command` in: whole command, use only if you really have to | yes | Called when a client command is parsed NOTE: hooks MUST start with if (MUTATOR_RETURNVALUE) return false; NOTE: return true if you handled the command, return false to continue handling NOTE: THESE HOOKS MUST NEVER EVER CALL tokenize() // example: MUTATOR_HOOKFUNCTION(foo, CSQC_ConsoleCommand) { if (MUTATOR_RETURNVALUE) return false; // command was already handled string cmd_name = M_ARGV(0, string); int cmd_argc = M_ARGV(1, int); string cmd_string = M_ARGV(2, string); if (cmd_name == "echocvar" && cmd_argc >= 2) { print(cvar_string(argv(1)), "\n"); return true; } if (cmd_name == "echostring" && cmd_argc >= 2) { print(substring(cmd_string, argv_start_index(1), argv_end_index(-1) - argv_start_index(1)), "\n"); return true; } return false; } |
